And there you have it! You’ve just put our LLM through a comprehensive privacy and security checkup. As you might see from this example, a vanilla LLM isn’t built for privacy and security, which means we have a long way to go, and an exciting journey together throughout this book!

就这样！你刚给 LLM 做完一次全面的隐私与安全体检。从这个例子可以看到，原生 LLM 并非为隐私和安全而生，我们还有很长的路要走——也意味着本书将带你走过一段精彩的旅程。

In this example, the LLMPrivacySecurityEvaluator is initialized with the Gemma model (a popular LLM by Google) and tokenizer. This example demonstrates how to use the LLMPrivacySecurityEvaluator class in a practical, fun way to evaluate the privacy and security risks of an LLM. By simulating different attack scenarios, you can get a comprehensive understanding of how vulnerable your model is to potential threats. This “clinic checkup” can be easily adapted to larger models and more complex scenarios as needed.

本例用 Google 的流行 LLM Gemma 及其 tokenizer 初始化评估器，以实用、有趣的方式演示如何用 LLMPrivacySecurityEvaluator 评估 LLM 的隐私与安全风险。通过模拟不同攻击场景，可以全面了解模型对潜在威胁的脆弱程度；这个“诊所体检”可以按需轻松迁移到更大的模型和更复杂的场景。

— PDF 第 103 页 —

Feel free to tweak parameters like n_attempts, threshold, and max_length to better suit your model and attack scenario. The more refined the attack, the higher the success rate.

可随意调整 n_attempts、threshold、max_length 等参数，以更好适配模型和攻击场景。攻击越精细，成功率往往越高。

As you will see in future chapters, the LLMPrivacySecurityEvaluator class can be a handy tool for assessing the privacy and security of large language models. Although you will not be evaluating all the classes of methods with it, you can use it to benchmark and compare different hyperparameters or method variants to choose the best configurations for your applications.

如后续章节所示，LLMPrivacySecurityEvaluator 是评估 LLM 隐私与安全的便捷工具。虽然不会用它评估所有方法类别，但可以用它做基准测试，比较不同超参数或方法变体，为应用选择最佳配置。

By incorporating multiple attack simulations, you can gain valuable insights into the vulnerabilities of your model and take proactive steps to mitigate potential privacy breaches. Whether you’re simulating membership inference, data extraction, or other types of attacks, this class serves as an all-in-one framework for conducting thorough security audits.

融入多种攻击模拟后，就能深入洞察模型漏洞，并主动采取措施缓解潜在隐私泄露。无论模拟成员推断、数据提取还是其他攻击，这个类都是开展彻底安全审计的一体化框架。

Different personas, different approaches 不同角色，不同方法

An important thing to note is that how you use these evaluation tools also depends significantly on your role in the LLM lifecycle.

需要注意的是，如何使用这些评估工具很大程度上取决于你在 LLM 生命周期中扮演的角色。

If you are a model creator or developer (with access to training data), you have the advantage of knowing exactly what data was used in training. What this means is that you can create targeted test cases using actual training examples and measure true membership inference accuracy (both false positives and false negatives). You should test with both real training examples and similar, but not included, examples. Your evaluation can serve as a definitive assessment of memorization risks.

如果你是模型创建者或开发者（能访问训练数据），优势是确切知道训练用了什么数据：可以用真实训练样本构造针对性测试用例，测量真实的成员推断准确率（包括假阳性和假阴性），同时用真实样本和相似但未参与训练的样本做测试，评估就能作为记忆风险的确切判定。

If you are a model user or practitioner (without access to training data), since you don’t know what data was actually used in training, your evaluation serves as a risk assessment rather than a definitive measurement. You should pay special attention to information relevant to your specific use case and industry, and focus on:

如果你是模型用户或从业者（无法访问训练数据），由于不知道实际训练数据，评估只能作为风险估计而非确切测量。应特别关注与自己用例和行业相关的信息，并聚焦于：

  • Testing with sensitive data from your domain that might be similar to training data

    用本领域可能与训练数据相似的敏感数据进行测试

  • Creating synthetic examples of the type of information you’re concerned about

    构造你所关心信息类型的合成示例

  • Using public information that likely appears in the training data as positive examples

    用很可能出现在训练数据中的公开信息作为正例

  • Creating canary examples (unique text you create) as negative examples

    构造你自己创造的唯一文本（金丝雀样本）作为负例

If you are a red-team security researcher, you can take an adversarial approach by crafting especially challenging prompts. By focusing on developing novel attack techniques that might bypass current defenses, you can help identify weaknesses in the

如果你是红队安全研究员，可以采取对抗思路，构造特别有挑战性的提示，专注开发可能绕过现有防御的新型攻击技术，帮助发现——

— PDF 第 104 页 —

model’s security. Your evaluation should include testing edge cases and unusual inputs that might not be covered by standard evaluations, looking for patterns in successful extractions to identify model vulnerabilities, and lastly, documenting and reporting findings to help improve model security.

模型安全中的弱点。评估应包括：测试标准评估未覆盖的边缘案例和异常输入；从成功提取中找模式以识别模型漏洞；最后记录并报告发现，帮助改进模型安全。

If you’re a practitioner without access to training data, consider creating a “proxy ground truth” by: 1. Generating a collection of test cases mixing public knowledge, industry-specific information, and synthetic examples; 2. Labeling them based on the likelihood of inclusion in training data (high, medium, low); 3. Measuring extraction success rates across these categories to estimate vulnerability. This approach won’t give you definitive answers but can provide valuable risk estimates for your specific use case.

如果你是无法访问训练数据的从业者，可以考虑构造“代理真值”：1. 生成一批混合公开知识、行业专属信息和合成示例的测试用例；2. 按它们出现在训练数据中的可能性（高、中、低）标注；3. 测量各类别下的提取成功率以估计脆弱程度。这种方法给不出确切答案，但能为你的具体用例提供有价值的风险估计。

Modern Evaluation Frameworks and Benchmarks 现代评估框架与基准

While our LLMPrivacySecurityEvaluator provides hands-on evaluation capabilities for you to customize, the field has developed several comprehensive frameworks and benchmarks for standardized LLM assessment. Understanding these tools helps you contextualize your results and compare against industry standards. Here are some recent ones.

LLMPrivacySecurityEvaluator 提供了可定制的动手评估能力，但学界业界还发展了若干用于标准化 LLM 评估的综合框架和基准。了解这些工具有助于把你的结果放在更大背景下、与行业标准比较。下面介绍几个近期的。

Holistic Evaluation of Language Models (HELM), developed by Stanford’s Center for Research on Foundation Models,1 provides a comprehensive framework for evaluating LLMs across multiple dimensions, including accuracy, calibration, robustness, fairness, bias, toxicity, and efficiency. It provides standardized scenarios and public leaderboards for comparing models and reproducible evaluation protocols.

HELM（语言模型整体评估）由斯坦福基础模型研究中心开发，提供跨多维度评估 LLM 的综合框架，涵盖准确性、校准、鲁棒性、公平、偏见、毒性和效率，提供标准化场景、公开排行榜和可复现的评估协议。

TruthfulQA measures whether language models are truthful in generating answers to questions.2 It’s particularly important for evaluating whether models propagate common misconceptions or generate plausible but false information. The benchmark includes 817 questions spanning 38 categories (health, law, finance, politics, etc.), which are designed to test the model’s ability to provide accurate and truthful responses.

TruthfulQA 衡量语言模型回答问题时是否诚实，对评估模型是否传播常见误解、或生成貌似合理实则错误的信息尤其重要。该基准含 817 个问题、横跨 38 个类别（医疗、法律、金融、政治等），用于测试模型给出准确、真实回答的能力。

1 Percy Liang et al., “Holistic Evaluation of Language Models,” arXiv preprint arXiv:2211.09110 (2022).

1 Percy Liang 等，《Holistic Evaluation of Language Models》，arXiv 预印本 arXiv:2211.09110（2022）。

2 Stephanie Lin, Jacob Hilton, and Owain Evans, “TruthfulQA: Measuring How Models Mimic Human Falsehoods,” in Proceedings of the 60th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers) (2022): 3214–3252.

2 Stephanie Lin、Jacob Hilton、Owain Evans，《TruthfulQA: Measuring How Models Mimic Human Falsehoods》，第 60 届计算语言学协会年会论文集（第 1 卷：长文）（2022）：3214–3252。

— PDF 第 105 页 —

HarmBench3 and JailbreakBench4 provide standardized evaluation for AI safety, specifically testing whether models can be manipulated to generate harmful content. These include a diverse set of harmful behaviors to test, automated and human evaluation methods, standardized jailbreaking attempts, and comparative results across models.

HarmBench 和 JailbreakBench 提供 AI 安全的标准化评估，专门测试模型是否会被操纵生成有害内容。它们包含多样的有害行为测试集、自动化与人工评估方法、标准化越狱尝试，以及跨模型的比较结果。

Although these benchmarks do not focus exclusively on privacy and security, they include important aspects relevant to these areas. For example, TruthfulQA’s emphasis on truthfulness helps assess whether models are likely to generate misleading or harmful information, which is a key security concern. Similarly, HELM’s robustness and bias evaluations can highlight vulnerabilities that could be exploited in adversarial attacks. This is particularly relevant for privacy and security because models that confidently generate false information pose serious risks in high-stakes applications.

这些基准虽不专门聚焦隐私与安全，但包含相关的重要方面：TruthfulQA 对真实性的强调有助于评估模型是否会生成误导或有害信息；HELM 的鲁棒性与偏见评估能揭示可能被对抗攻击利用的漏洞。这与隐私安全尤其相关，因为自信生成错误信息的模型在高风险应用中会造成严重后果。

In Chapters 7 and 8, you will explore these socio-technical and ethical dimensions in more detail, especially their implications for responsible and safe AI development.

第 7、8 章将更详细探讨这些社会技术与伦理维度，尤其是它们对负责任、安全的 AI 开发的意义。

Lastly, while not an evaluation framework per se, the AI Incident Database catalogs real-world AI failures and harms. Reviewing these incidents helps inform you what to test for in your own evaluations.

最后，AI 事件数据库虽不是评估框架本身，但它记录了真实世界的 AI 故障与危害，复盘这些事件有助于你确定自己的评估该测什么。

When using standardized benchmarks: Understand that good benchmark scores don’t guarantee real-world safety; Benchmarks may become outdated as attack techniques evolve; Combine standardized benchmarks with domain-specific evaluations; Consider adversarial variants of benchmarks that test robustness, not just capabilities; Remember that models can be specifically optimized for benchmarks (Goodhart’s Law applies).

使用标准化基准时请注意：基准分数高并不保证真实世界安全；攻击技术演进后基准可能过时；把标准化基准与领域专属评估结合；考虑测试鲁棒性而非仅能力的对抗变体基准；记住模型可能被专门针对基准优化（古德哈特定律在此适用）。

3 Mantas Mazeika et al., “HarmBench: A Standardized Evaluation Framework for Automated Red Teaming and Robust Refusal,” in Proceedings of the 41st International Conference on Machine Learning (2024): 35181–35224.

3 Mantas Mazeika 等，《HarmBench: A Standardized Evaluation Framework for Automated Red Teaming and Robust Refusal》，第 41 届国际机器学习会议论文集（2024）：35181–35224。

4 Patrick Chao et al., “Jailbreakbench: An Open Robustness Benchmark for Jailbreaking Large Language Models,” Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 37 (2024): 55005–55029.

4 Patrick Chao 等，《Jailbreakbench: An Open Robustness Benchmark for Jailbreaking Large Language Models》，《神经信息处理系统进展》37（2024）：55005–55029。

Summary 本章小结

As you’ve seen, evaluating the privacy and security of LLMs is a bit like being a sheriff in the Wild West of AI. You’ve got your trusty metrics as your six-shooters, helping you fend off privacy breaches and security attacks. But just like in the Old West, the landscape is always changing, and new threats are always emerging.

如你所见，评估 LLM 的隐私与安全有点像在 AI 的西部世界当警长：你手握指标这把六响枪，抵御隐私泄露和安全攻击。但正如老西部，地形永远在变，新威胁层出不穷。

Jokes aside, it’s crucial to remember that no model is ever completely secure or private. Our goal is to make it as hard as possible for attackers to succeed while maintaining the utility of our models. By regularly evaluating your models using the techniques we’ve discussed, you can stay one step ahead of potential threats.

玩笑归玩笑，必须记住：没有模型是绝对安全或私密的。我们的目标是在保持模型效用的同时，让攻击者尽可能难得手。用本章讨论的技术定期评估模型，就能比潜在威胁快一步。

For this purpose, you’ve built a hands-on framework for evaluating the privacy and security risks of LLMs. We started by exploring fundamental privacy metrics—differential privacy, privacy loss, and k-anonymity—each providing different lenses through which to assess how well your models protect sensitive information. These mathematical frameworks give you rigorous ways to quantify privacy risks and set acceptable bounds for information leakage.

为此，你搭建了一套评估 LLM 隐私与安全风险的动手框架：从基础隐私指标——差分隐私、隐私损失、k-匿名——入手，它们各从不同视角衡量模型对敏感信息的保护程度，这些数学框架让你能严格量化隐私风险并设定可接受的信息泄露界。

You then examined security metrics including Attack Success Rate, False Positive Rate for membership inference attacks, and reconstruction errors for model inversion attacks. These metrics help us understand not just whether attacks are possible, but how often they succeed and how accurately they can reconstruct sensitive information. By combining privacy and security metrics, you can develop a holistic view of model vulnerabilities.

接着考察了安全指标：攻击成功率、成员推断的假阳性率、模型反演的重建误差。这些指标不仅告诉我们攻击是否可能，还说明攻击多久成功一次、能多准确地重建敏感信息。把隐私与安全指标结合起来，就能形成对模型漏洞的整体认识。

A critical addition to our evaluation toolkit was understanding emerging attack vectors that represent the cutting edge of LLM security research. Prompt injection attacks exploit the model’s natural language understanding to override intended behavior, while jailbreaking techniques specifically target safety guardrails. Model extraction attempts to steal intellectual property by replicating model functionality, and training data poisoning can compromise models before they’re even deployed. Understanding these evolving threats is essential because new attack methods emerge as quickly as defenses are developed.

评估工具包中关键的一环是了解代表 LLM 安全研究前沿的新兴攻击向量：提示注入利用模型的自然语言理解覆盖预期行为；越狱专门针对安全护栏；模型提取通过复制模型功能窃取知识产权；训练数据投毒则在模型部署前就将其 compromising。理解这些不断演进的威胁至关重要，因为新攻击方法出现的速度和防御被研发出来的速度一样快。

To truly understand LLM vulnerabilities, other than the public benchmarks mentioned earlier, several platforms allow you to practice “hacking” LLMs in a safe, controlled environment, such as Gandalf by Lakera—a popular game where you try to extract a secret password from an LLM named Gandalf—and HackAPrompt—a competitive platform where you can test your skills against increasingly difficult prompts and compare your performance with others.

要真正理解 LLM 漏洞，除了前面提到的公开基准，还有若干平台让你在安全可控的环境中练习“黑掉” LLM：例如 Lakera 出品的 Gandalf——一个流行游戏，目标是从名为 Gandalf 的 LLM 中提取秘密密码；以及 HackAPrompt——一个竞赛平台，用难度递增的提示考验你的技巧并与他人比较成绩。

— PDF 第 107 页 —

Here are some key takeaways:

本章要点：

  • Privacy and security in LLMs are multifaceted issues. There’s no single metric that captures everything.

    LLM 的隐私与安全是多层面的问题，没有哪个单一指标能概括一切。

  • Differential privacy techniques can help protect individual privacy, but there’s often a trade-off with utility.

    差分隐私技术有助于保护个人隐私，但往往与效用存在权衡。

  • Security against attacks like membership inference and data extraction is crucial, especially as LLMs are deployed in sensitive domains.

    抵御成员推断、数据提取等攻击的安全措施至关重要，尤其当 LLM 部署于敏感领域时。

  • Regular audits using tools like our LLMPrivacySecurityEvaluator can help identify potential vulnerabilities.

    用 LLMPrivacySecurityEvaluator 这类工具定期审计，有助于发现潜在漏洞。

  • As LLM technology evolves, so too must our evaluation techniques. Stay vigilant and keep learning!

    随着 LLM 技术演进，评估技术也必须演进。保持警惕、持续学习！

The chapter also highlighted how your role shapes evaluation strategy. Model creators with training data access can perform definitive assessments, while practitioners without such access must rely on risk estimates and proxy ground truth. Security researchers take an adversarial approach, probing for novel vulnerabilities that might bypass current defenses. Understanding these different perspectives helps you design evaluations appropriate to your situation and constraints.

本章还强调了你的角色如何塑造评估策略：能访问训练数据的模型创建者可以做确切评估；无法访问的从业者只能依赖风险估计和代理真值；安全研究员则采取对抗思路，探测可能绕过现有防御的新型漏洞。理解这些不同视角，有助于设计适合自身处境和约束的评估。

Now that you’ve established comprehensive methods for evaluating privacy and security risks, you’re ready to move beyond diagnosis to treatment. In the next chapter, you’ll explore privacy-preserving training techniques that let you build these protections directly into your models from the start. After all, an ounce of prevention is worth a pound of cure, especially when it comes to AI security.

既然已经建立了评估隐私与安全风险的完整方法，就可以从“诊断”走向“治疗”了。下一章将探讨隐私保护训练技术，让你从一开始就把保护机制直接构建进模型——毕竟，预防胜于治疗，在 AI 安全领域尤其如此。
